title: Bridgeway Labs - edge split-horizon & LLM dataflow discovery
summary: Discovery focused on how Bridgeway's LLM inference traffic should be routed from regional edge nodes into Redwood Private. Customer has EU data residency constraints and a multi-region edge footprint. Key decision: VPC peering + Transit GW vs Private Endpoints for predictable latency and IP control. Action: network workshop and exchange diagrams, Redwood to send private deployment checklist, pricing options.
next_steps: Redwood to send private deployment pricing and Dedicated vs Private comparison (Maya)
Schedule network workshop with Bridgeway network team (Liam + Bridgeway NOC)
Customer to share VPC diagrams and list of egress IP constraints (Alejandra)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send Private deployment pricing + short comparison doc (due 2026-01-11)
Liam O'Connor: Prepare network checklist and sample Terraform for Private endpoints and Transit Gateway (due 2026-01-15)
Rina Shah: Share Bridgeway's SOC2 audit contact and KMS requirements (due 2026-01-12)
Tom Patel: Provide current edge PoP list and typical RPS / token throughput peaks (due 2026-01-12)
transcript: 00:00:00 - Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. we have about 45 minutes, agenda is quick net intake, constraints, and then dig into architecture options.

00:00:12 - Alejandra Ruiz: Great, thanks Maya. Quick background — Bridgeway runs an inference mesh across eu/west and eu/north edge PoPs, data residency requires all inference requests for EU customers stay in eu regions. we're evaluating Redwood Private to avoid public egress and want low latency from edge to model.
00:00:35 - Tom Patel: Also, we have some split-horizon routing in place — internal customers route differently than public facing, so our ask is how Redwood would fit with that.
00:00:50 - Maya Chen: Perfect. Liam, want to take us through the two high level patterns we recommend?

00:00:55 - Liam O'Connor: Yeah, sure. Two main patterns: VPC peering / Transit Gateway where your VPCs peer to Redwood's private VPCs, or Private Endpoints (privatelink-style) where we expose an endpoint per region. Peering gives full L3 control and predictable IPs, endpoints are simpler from a security posture but can be trickier for some split-horizon setups.
00:01:22 - Rina Shah: When you say predictable IPs, do you mean static egress IP blocks we can allowlist?

00:01:27 - Liam O'Connor: With Dedicated/Private you can have a small set of egress IP prefixes for the service plane, yes. For peering + Transit GW we can work with your network team to carve subnets. We also have options to support NAT or no-NAT depending on routing requirements.
00:01:48 - Benji Moore: Our big concern is latency spikes during bursts. We need consistent 50–100 ms p95 from our edge PoPs to the model for short-text classification. any guidance there?

00:01:58 - Liam O'Connor: 50–100 ms is feasible with regional placement and avoiding unnecessary hairpinning. If you colocate Redwood Private in the same cloud region as your edge aggregator and use direct peering, that tends to be the lowest latency. Also continuous batching configs can help throughput without adding much tail latency.
00:02:22 - Alejandra Ruiz: We also have strict EU-only data residency. can Redwood guarantee that data and KV cache stay within eu-west-1 / eu-north-1?
00:02:34 - Maya Chen: Yes — for Private deployments you can pick regions and we will pin model serving and caching to those regions. We'll include region lock options in the deployment plan.

00:02:45 - Tom Patel: A bit more on split-horizon: Our edge returns internal service traffic over a private backbone but external user traffic routes over Internet. we want internal dev/test calls to hit staging model variants and prod calls to hit prod model variants in the same region. Does Redwood support route-based environment segregation?

00:03:07 - Liam O'Connor: We do policy-based routing at request-time — routing rules can pick model versions by headers, tokens, or source CIDR. If your split-horizon maps to separate source CIDR ranges, we can wire a policy that sends internal CIDR to the staging cluster. There's some config work on route tables and security groups to ensure the right egress path.
00:03:34 - Rina Shah: Security-wise, what about KMS/HSM integration for encryption at rest and audit logs? We need to validate with our compliance team.
00:03:43 - Maya Chen: For Private we support customer-managed KMS keys and will export audit logs. Liam, do you want to add specifics?

00:03:49 - Liam O'Connor: Sure. We integrate with cloud KMS (customer keys) for model artifacts and KV cache encryption in transit and at rest. Audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM via a closed VPC endpoint. there may be small differences between cloud providers but we have an enterprise security pack we can share.

00:04:16 - Alejandra Ruiz: Is there a difference in network footprint between Dedicated capacity and Private? we heard Dedicated is multi-tenant but isolated compute. wondering if that affects egress control.

00:04:29 - Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity inside Redwood's environment — you get dedicated GPU pools and logical isolation, but the control plane remains on our hosted layer. Private (VPC) gives you full network isolation and control plane connectors can be deployed into your VPC. If strict egress and no managed control plane access is required, Private is the path.
00:04:51 - Tom Patel: So for our EU-only requirement + split-horizon + allowlisting, Private sounds right. what are the practical networking choices?

00:04:59 - Liam O'Connor: Practically: 1) Transit Gateway peering — we peer to your Transit GW and you propagate routes to edge PoPs; 2) VPC peering per region — simpler but more peering entries; 3) Private Endpoints — Reduces routing complexity but you need endpoint connectivity from edge PoPs. For split-horizon many customers prefer Transit GW because it's easiest to centralize routing and apply firewall policies.
00:05:30 - Benji Moore: Do you support IP-based allowlists for model-serving endpoints? e.g., a fixed /24 we can rely on?

00:05:36 - Liam O'Connor: Yes. We'll provide the expected IP ranges per region. For Private deployments those can be under your control if we deploy within your account — then you control the subnets. If we host the Private nodes in Redwood account, we provide stable egress ranges.
00:06:04 - Alejandra Ruiz: any gotchas with split-horizon and TLS SNI? we want to terminate TLS at the edge and forward to model nodes internally.

00:06:13 - Liam O'Connor: Terminating at the edge is fine. We recommend preserving a routing header or JWT so the model cluster can determine environment. SNI should be fine as long as the TLS session gets forwarded. If you need mutual TLS between edge and Redwood, we support mTLS via certs or client TLS.
00:06:36 - Tom Patel: What about cross-account peering if we want Redwood in our account?

00:06:41 - Maya Chen: We have a model where Redwood can deploy Private connectors into customer accounts — in that case routing is fully within your account and you control SGs/subnets. SE to follow up with Terraform examples.
00:06:58 - Rina Shah: latency SLO during bursts — if we push 5k rps during a marketing event, how do we avoid cold-start/queueing?

00:07:07 - Liam O'Connor: We can size Dedicated pools with buffer capacity and autoscaling. For Private, you control autoscaling policies; we provide guidance on instance types, warm pools, and pre-warming. We also recommend caching and batching for classification style calls. For very spiky workloads, a small warm standby pool reduces cold starts.
00:07:34 - Benji Moore: any differences in feature parity between Private and Hosted? like streaming or tool-calling?

00:07:40 - Maya Chen: Feature parity is strong — streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings, all supported. Occasionally a new hosted-only feature may lag in Private by a short dev window but we sync quickly.
00:07:54 - Alejandra Ruiz: On the compliance side we need SOC2 Type II, ISO-27001 evidence, and an option for HSM-backed keys. can you provide that?
00:08:04 - Maya Chen: Yes. We'll share our compliance pack and HSM/KMS integration notes. Liam will add contact and specific artifacts.

00:08:12 - Liam O'Connor: I'll drop the compliance pack link and a network checklist. Also sample Terraform modules for setting up VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll also include examples for split-horizon route table entries.
00:08:30 - Alejandra Ruiz: about peering and egress— we have strict egress IP allowlists for third-party services. will Redwood's control plane ever egress to non-eu telemetry endpoints?

00:08:42 - Maya Chen: For Private we can arrange to keep telemetry in-region; we will need to understand which telemetry you want forwarded. We also have options to ship logs to your SIEM rather than to our hosted analytics. We'll note that as part of the checklist.
00:09:00 - Tom Patel: Are there costs for transit gateway attachments or cross-AZ traffic we should model?

00:09:07 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, cloud vendor transit costs apply. We'll provide an estimate template — network egress and transit are billed by the cloud provider and should be included in your TCO. Redwood pricing doc will show compute/token costs; network costs are separate.
00:09:25 - Benji Moore: Do you have any customers who run split-horizon and region lock? curious for references or an architecture doc.
00:09:33 - Maya Chen: We do, happy to share an anonymized architecture doc and a short case study. We'll link it in follow up.
00:09:41 - Alejandra Ruiz: Great. One more thing: we rely heavily on internal tracing and x-forwarded-for to map requests to tenants. can Redwood preserve those headers?
00:09:50 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can pass through x-forwarded-* headers or strip and re-inject based on policy. We also support per-token tagging for billing/attribution.

00:10:05 - Maya Chen: quick recap: Bridgeway needs EU-only hosting, split-horizon routing support for dev/prod, stable egress IPs for allowlisting, and low p95 latency. Next steps: we'll send pricing & private deployment checklist, Liam will run a network workshop and provide Terraform examples, and Bridgeway will share diagrams and constraints. Any other blockers?
00:10:25 - Alejandra Ruiz: timeline: ideally pilot in the next 6 weeks, production rollout in Q2 if POC goes well. budget is flexible but needs to include network transit costs.
00:10:36 - Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. we'll follow up with proposed pilot scope and a network workshop invite. Thank you all.
00:10:42 - Tom Patel: thanks, appreciate it.
00:10:44 - Rina Shah: thank you.
